subject: Request: execution locations, subprocessor responsibilities, and deletion SLA — Polaris Payments Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Berger <alex.berger@polaris-pay.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick Qs on where requests execute and deletion timeline

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week. Two quick questions the security team asked that I couldn't answer: 1) For customer requests to your hosted API, in which cloud regions and by which subprocessors are those requests executed? 2) If we ask for deletion of customer data (or a subset), what is the end-to-end timeline and which parties are involved?

We're trying to confirm that none of our EU-origin traffic leaves EU-controlled processing without contractual safeguards. Can you send a short summary (or pointer to a diagram) and any SLA/commitments we can include in our procurement review?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call.

Best,
Alex Berger
Head of Infrastructure Security
Polaris Payments
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Berger <alex.berger@polaris-pay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-02T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests execute and deletion timeline

Alex —

Thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below; attaching a simple diagram and our current subprocessor CSV for your review. If you'd like a signed attestation we can escalate that through our security team (see next steps).

1) Execution regions:
- For EU-origin traffic to our hosted API, requests are routed to EU compute by default (we operate in eu-central-1 and eu-west-2 regions).
- Routing policy: we route by request geo-ip + billing tenant config. Customers can pin to EU-only execution in contract.

2) Subprocessors and roles:
- Our front door/load balancing is run by Redwood-managed cloud accounts; primary subprocessors are: CloudProviderEU (IaaS), CDNPartner (edge caching), and MetricsVendor (telemetry).
- The attached inventory lists subprocessors and whether they receive request payloads or only telemetry/metrics. Most EU requests do not cross outside EU except for certain operational telemetry which is pseudonymized.

3) Deletion flow & SLA:
- Deletion request received via API or support ticket -> validated (0-4 hours) -> queued for purge job (within 24 hours) -> purge executed across caches/kv/long-term stores (48–72 hours depending on outstanding cache window) -> final audit log entry delivered to customer (within 5 business days).
- Parties involved: Redwood runtime (purge), CloudProviderEU (physical storage operations), and SRE team (audit verification). Subprocessors are contractually required to follow deletion instructions within our agreed timelines.

Next steps: if you need per-subprocessor DPA clauses or export-control wording (e.g., EU data never transferred to non-EU subprocessors), flag that and we'll coordinate legal.

Attachments: residency_architecture_diagram.pdf (diagram), subprocessor_inventory_aug2027.csv (spreadsheet).

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Berger <alex.berger@polaris-pay.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-02T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests execute and deletion timeline

Alex — adding a couple of concrete bullets from ops:
- Edge caching (CDNPartner) only holds encrypted prefixes and is configured with TTLs under 1 hour for session-like traffic; we include cache purge APIs in the delete flow.
- KV caches live on dedicated EU instances; eviction plus explicit purge ensures keys are removed within 48h.
- Long-term blob storage snapshots exist for backups — backups are retained for 30 days by default; deletion requests trigger shadow-erase and next-retention-cycle purge; we can shorten this with a contractual SLA to 7 days.

If Polaris needs a shorter backup-hold, let us know and we can propose an amendable retention clause.

-rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@polaris-pay.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alex Berger <alex.berger@polaris-pay.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T08:41:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: EU-only contractual restriction and attestations

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the fast response. Two follow-ups: 1) We need explicit contractual language that commits EU-origin traffic to EU-only execution and that no EU-origin raw payloads will be accessible to non-EU subprocessors. 2) Can you provide a short attestation (signed PDF) that outlines the deletion SLA and the people/processes involved?

Also, can you confirm whether any telemetry/metrics sent to MetricsVendor include raw request text? Our compliance team flagged that as a potential exception.

Thanks — Sophie
Head of Privacy, Polaris Payments
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@polaris-pay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-04T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: EU-only contractual restriction and attestations

Sophie —

Appreciate the specifics. Confirmations below and proposed next actions:

Confirmations:
- EU-only execution: yes. We support an EU-only execution option that can be added to the DPA; once enabled, routing and model execution occur on EU-bound compute exclusively. We will not route raw EU-origin request payloads to non-EU subprocessors.
- Telemetry to MetricsVendor: we send aggregated metrics and pseudonymized telemetry by default. Raw request text is NOT sent to MetricsVendor unless explicitly enabled in an integration; that is a customer opt-in.
- Deletion attestation: we can provide a signed attestation PDF. Standard internal timeline matches what I outlined earlier (final audit within 5 business days). For purchase/contract, we can commit to a customized deletion SLA (e.g., 7 days end-to-end) as a commercial term.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Legal to prepare a DPA snippet for EU-only execution and an attestation PDF (target: 3 business days).
2) Marissa and Rishi will prepare an operations note describing backup retention and purge mechanics (attached CSV shows current state).
3) If helpful, we'll set a 30-min call with your privacy team to walk the diagram and signoff.

If Polaris wants the backup window shortened contractually, indicate desired SLA and I'll include it in the proposal.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
